target_customer: Regulated businesses (fintech, banks, gambling, telecom) needing KYC and AML identity checks
problem: Verifying customer identity across countries means many local methods. Authologic aggregates video, bank data and government eIDs behind one API.
business_model: Usage-based API and SaaS for identity verification

founders.name: Krzysztof Klimczak
prior_employers: Societe Generale Poland (IT specialist, Head of IT Exploitation, Deputy CIO, 1995 to 2006)
previous_startups: ZenCard (2013 to 2020, sold in 2017 to the biggest Polish bank per his YC bio)

founders.name: Jarek Sygitowicz
founders.role: Co-founder, client relations, design and UX
founders.background_notes: YC page, which is inconsistent on who bought ZenCard

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrating many national eID and bank-based verification schemes plus biometrics is integration heavy and compliance sensitive, but uses known methods.

defensibility.rationale: Coverage of many local eID schemes and AML compliance take time to build and customers embed the API, but global vendors can add similar integrations.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Onfido was acquired by Entrust in Feb 2024 per a roundup; no incumbent bought Authologic.

market_need_then: EU AML rules and growth of online fintech required remote customer verification, and the founders ran ZenCard and Toyota Financial Services Poland where AML was their responsibility (YC page).

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and direct with short punchy sentences, urgency on AI fraud and regulation (company site).

branding.brand_signature: 'Stripe for online identity verification' positioning (YC page)
branding.community_and_virality: None found; trade press covered funding only.

brand_strength.rationale: Name combines auth and logic, and is confusable with Authlogics, an unrelated firm; no press on the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Authologic raised a small pre-seed in 2020, joined YC in Winter 2021 and closed an 8.2 million dollar Series A led by OpenOcean in October 2024 with offices in Warsaw, London and San Francisco. Experienced founders from a prior fintech exit, EU eID regulation and AML demand drove progress, while global verification vendors remain much better funded.
notes: Series A reported by Tech.eu, Finextra and Biometric Update; some outlets quote EUR 7.6M (Vestbee). The pre-seed is PLN 1.8M (about $460K) per Ain.ua and Nordic9. CB Insights shows $8.79M over six rounds; other rounds not identified. Education of founders not found. Competitors left empty because only 2026 roundups were found, none dated near the batch. Series A date is the Tech.eu article date.
